brief.headline: Tech bifurcation widens as crude drops 8% and breadth stays thin
brief.regime_summary: SPY sits at 761.69, just 0.5% above its 50-DMA and up 6.9% on the 200-DMA, with a 1-week return of -0.09%. Conditions are neutral, not trending. VIX at 14.87 is below its 20-DMA of 15.66, so realized fear is subdued, but that flatters the picture. Only 3 of 11 sectors hold above their 50-DMAs. Momentum is concentrated: XLK is the only sector positive on a 20-day basis (+3.5%); everything from XLF to XLU is negative, with defensive and rate-sensitive names especially weak. In this tape, breakouts in tech carry real leadership weight, but the narrow breadth means they lack broad confirmation. Treat strength selectively and size accordingly.

portfolio.note: Price at 493.78, 0.75% below the 20-DMA and 4.6% off the 20-day high. RSI 53, 20-day momentum +2.6%, MA stack remains bullish. No earnings until October 28. No action needed at current levels; watch 20-DMA at roughly 497 as near-term resistance.

Price at 1679.92, 6.2% off the 20-day high, 20-day momentum -4.0%, and the MA stack has flipped to mixed. Trailing P/E of 57.8 sits 47% above its historical median. A Barchart piece this weekend cited AI-slowdown calls from Amodei, Altman and Musk as a specific demand risk for lithography equipment. Earnings on October 14 are the next binary event; the setup warrants a fresh look at position sizing before then.

XLE at 64.31, down 1.3% on the week, but still 0.3% above its 20-DMA with a bullish MA stack. WTI fell 8.2% this week to 93.09; if crude does not stabilize near its 20-DMA, XLE's thin 20-day momentum of +0.9% will erode quickly. Watch for a WTI close below 92 as the signal that the XLE stack is at risk.

GLD at 401.17, up 0.6% on the week, MA stack bullish, RSI 51. Gold futures 20-day momentum is -6.3%, and GLD itself is 1.3% below its 20-DMA, so the near-term trend has stalled. The 40-day momentum of +8% and the bullish stack argue for patience unless the 40-DMA breaks.

watchlist.name: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.
watchlist.thesis: AMD surged 8.5% last week and is now 14.1% above its 20-DMA, sitting essentially at its 20-day high (559.82 vs. high of 559.91). RSI is 65.4, 20-day momentum is +19.3%, and it leads both sector and market on 20-day relative strength (+15.7% vs. XLK, +19.1% vs. SPY). Forward P/E of 36x is more reasonable than the trailing 143x, and CY EPS growth is estimated at 82%. A China summit is in focus this week per IBD, which could be a catalyst or a risk given AMD's exposure to export controls.
watchlist.levels: 20-DMA: ~490.75. 20-day high: 559.91. ATR-based stop distance: ~24.00 (4.3% of price).
watchlist.risk: Any negative development on chip export controls to China, or a pullback below the 20-DMA, breaks the momentum thesis given the extended distance from the average.

watchlist.name: CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc.
watchlist.thesis: CRWD rose 15.0% last week, the strongest weekly return in the screen. Price at 237.65 is 10.1% above the 20-DMA of 215.86 and 28.9% above the 100-DMA. RSI is 60.4, not yet overbought. 20-day relative strength is +21.3% vs. XLK and +24.7% vs. SPY. Revenue growth this year is estimated at 24.8% with 47 analyst EPS upgrades in 30 days vs. 1 downgrade. The 20-day high is 250.32, so there is still 5.3% of room before a new all-time high test.
watchlist.levels: 20-DMA: ~215.86. 20-day high: 250.32. ATR-based stop distance: ~12.85 (5.4% of price).
watchlist.risk: The trailing P/E is essentially infinite at 4,753x; any revenue guide miss at the December 1 earnings will be punished severely given valuation dependence on growth.

watchlist.name: Salesforce, Inc.
watchlist.thesis: CRM at 237.92 is the top-scoring screen name at 1.94. Trailing P/E of 21.8x sits 46% below its historical median of 40x. EPS trend over 30 days is +18.5%, with 45 upward revisions and zero downward. 40-day momentum is +51.9%. The stock pulled back 3.8% this week to 2.0% below the 20-DMA, creating a potential re-entry level into a structurally strong setup. Earnings are not until December 2.
watchlist.levels: 20-DMA: ~242.83. 20-day high: 267.80. ATR-based stop distance: ~9.64 (4.1% of price).
watchlist.risk: Price is below the 20-DMA; a failure to reclaim it on volume would suggest the pullback is more than a routine consolidation given high 20-day vol of 80.5%.

watchlist.name: Intel Corporation
watchlist.thesis: INTC gained 5.5% last week and sits 13.3% above its 20-DMA. CY EPS growth estimate of 262% is the highest on the screen. The MA stack is mixed (100-DMA still above shorter-term averages), which limits confidence, but 20-day relative strength vs. SPY is +17.8%. Earnings are October 22, so the window to trade the setup is limited.
watchlist.levels: 20-DMA: ~96.00 (implied by 13.3% gap from 108.60). 20-day high: ~111.30 (2.5% above price). ATR-based stop distance: ~5.84 (5.4% of price).
watchlist.risk: Mixed DMA stack and earnings on October 22 compress the risk/reward timeline; any negative pre-announcement or macro news on foundry subsidies breaks the setup.

watchlist.name: Nike, Inc.
watchlist.thesis: NKE at 35.51 hit 52-week lows last week and is in a full bearish MA stack, 6.2% below the 20-DMA and 14.6% below the 100-DMA. RSI is 32.8, approaching oversold but not yet bouncing. CY EPS growth is -19.4% with 5 analyst downgrades in 30 days vs. 1 upgrade. Baird downgraded both NKE and Dick's this week, citing a failed sportswear recovery thesis. Earnings are October 1, ten days away, raising event risk on either side.
watchlist.levels: 20-DMA: ~37.85. 20-day high: 40.91. ATR-based stop distance: ~0.98 (2.8% of price).
watchlist.risk: RSI near 30 and a deeply depressed price mean a positive earnings surprise or guidance lift on October 1 could trigger a sharp short-covering rally.

watchlist.name: Comcast Corporation
watchlist.thesis: CMCSA dropped 9.8% last week to 22.74, the worst weekly return in the screen. Price is 11.6% below its 20-DMA and 16.9% off its 20-day high. RSI is 29.7, technically oversold. 20-day momentum is -13.9%, relative strength vs. market is -14.1%. EPS revisions are negative (-0.29%) with EPS growth -18.8% this year. No specific catalyst in the news flow explains the move, which increases the chance the sell-off reflects information not yet public. Earnings on October 22 are the next known event.
watchlist.levels: 20-DMA: ~25.72 (implied by -11.6% gap). 20-day high: ~27.33 (implied by -16.9% gap). ATR-based stop distance: ~0.73 (3.2% of price).
watchlist.risk: Oversold RSI at 29.7 and a 9.8% single-week drop mean a technical bounce is possible at any point; a short setup requires clear stop discipline above the 20-DMA.

commodities.name: WTI Crude
commodities.note: Fell 8.2% last week to 93.09, the largest decline in the commodity screen. Price is flat against its 20-DMA but 12.8% off the 20-day high and ATR is 4.8% of price. Watch whether 92-93 holds as a floor; a break would threaten XLE's MA stack and widen the portfolio loss on that position.

commodities.name: Copper
commodities.note: Copper rose 7.2% last week to 6.785 on volume nearly 4x the average, a breakout-on-volume signal. RSI is 61, 20-day momentum is +3.1%, and price is only 0.3% from the 20-day high. This is the strongest commodity setup in the screen and worth watching as a leading indicator for global industrial demand.

commodities.name: Gold
commodities.note: Gold futures at 4386.70, up 0.8% on the week but 2.0% below the 20-DMA and 7.8% off the 20-day high. The 20-day momentum is -6.3%, suggesting near-term distribution even as the long structure (40-day +7.8%) remains intact. GLD holders should watch the 40-DMA for any break.

commodities.name: Corn
commodities.note: Corn rose 4.1% last week to 532.75, RSI at 69.5 and only 1.2% below the 20-day high. The 20-day momentum is +10.1% and the MA stack is fully bullish. Approaching overbought; worth monitoring for a potential continuation or stall given the nearly 70 RSI reading.

commodities.name: Silver
commodities.note: Silver gained 4.8% last week to 66.55 on volume nearly 6x the 20-day average, a significant volume spike. RSI is 54.6, and the 40-day momentum is +13.5%. The MA stack is mixed (below 100-DMA by 0.3%), so the move is compelling but not yet structurally confirmed.

risks: WTI crude fell 8.2% in one week; if the move continues, energy earnings estimates for Q4 face meaningful cuts and XLE's bullish stack breaks.
Breadth is critically thin: only 3 of 11 sectors above their 50-DMAs. The tech rally is carrying the index. Any tech-specific shock (export controls, earnings warning) has outsized index impact.
ASML earnings October 14: AI-slowdown narrative from top lab CEOs is a specific demand-side risk for lithography equipment. Position is 104.9% in profit; pre-earnings sizing is worth reviewing.
NKE earnings October 1 and INTC earnings October 22 both arrive before the next brief cycle. Both names are in extended moves (NKE down, INTC up) and gap risk is elevated.
Copper's 7.2% weekly surge on 4x volume may be signaling a demand reacceleration, but if it reverses sharply it would be a bearish divergence signal for cyclicals and materials.
